 You are here: Home / News / National News / Lawmakers renew push for a federal Diwali holiday Lawmakers renew push for a federal Diwali holiday
 November 19, 2026 By Admin Leave a Comment 
 The chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus has reintroduced the Diwali Day Act to recognize Diwali as a federal holiday. 
 Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, is one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists as well as billions in the South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities.  
 “Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognizing Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society,” said CAPAC Chair Rep. Grace Meng.
 Hindu and South Asian communities across the country are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation, and targeted violence. This includes vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and the recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Seattle.  
 Under Meng’s legislation, Diwali would become the 12th federally recognized holiday in the United States. Meng is also the author of the Lunar New Year Day Act, which would establish Lunar New Year as a federally recognized holiday. 
 This bill is co-sponsored by 19 members of Congress, including Rep. Suzan DelBene of Washington.
